## Eight common assumptions, negated

| # | Assumption practitioners usually hold | If it were false, what conditional effect would follow |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | A 0→3 residual makes the main path's operations less critical. | A skip on edge 3 would make the receptive field on the main path *more* critical, so 3x3→1x1 downgrades on edges 4 and 5 would hurt more under it. Conversely, a conv shortcut that already supplies a 3x3 receptive field would buffer those downgrades. |
| A2 | Edge-3 conv and edge-3 skip are independently good, whatever else is in the cell. | The best edge-3 op would depend on the main path. A conv shortcut would pay off mainly when the path into node 3 is parameter-free. A skip shortcut would pay off mainly when that path is a strong conv. |
| A3 | Extra depth (0→1→2→3) only matters for restoring connectivity. | Adding a conv on edge 2 would bring a gain beyond connectivity. That gain would be largest when edge 4 is pruned, so the deep path stops competing with the shallow 1→3 route. |
| A4 | Parallel conv routes into the same node add up. | They would substitute for each other. A conv on edge 1 or edge 2 would gain less when the other one is already a conv. |
| A5 | "Too many skips hurt" depends only on the count, not on where the skips sit. | Skips converging on node 3 (edges 3 and 5) would be much worse than skips placed upstream. |
| A6 | Pooling on an output edge is uniformly mild. | Its penalty would depend on what else feeds node 3. Learned features from a conv shortcut would absorb it, and an identity upstream would amplify it. |
| A7 | Edge 4 behaves the same whatever edge 0 does. | Edge 4 would inherit node 1's quality. A skip on edge 4 would be valuable when node 1 is a conv output, and redundant when node 1 is the identity. |
| A8 | Effects of edges near node 3 are independent of whether the cell has another output route. | When edge 3 or edge 4 is `none`, the remaining output edges would become bottlenecks, and their edits would matter more. |

**Constraints applied to the hypotheses below:**
- The second gap as stated (k = j = 3) is a banned same-field condition. I recast it as the edge-3 edits in H4, H5, H6 and H14, which condition on the *main* path instead.
- No condition is the same field as the edit, and no condition makes the edited edge inert.
- No condition setting appears more than twice.
